_description: Conformance vectors for traigent_schema/content_identity.py, the R3 dataset-version content digest and evaluator judge-config digest. Both digests layer the certification family's role-digest construction (sha256(UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || jcs_v1(payload))) on top of fp2 (fp2's own corpus is tests/data/fp2_conformance.json and is untouched by this file). Every expected_digest here was generated by running the actual functions, not hand-computed.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: two_example_set
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: Baseline two-example set; the reordered/one_byte/no_expected/dup_ids/empty vectors below are all deliberate variations on this one.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: two_example_set_reordered
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: Same two examples as two_example_set, supplied in reverse order. Must equal two_example_set's digest: sorting by example_id is part of the projection, so caller order is not observable.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: two_example_set_one_byte_change
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: Same as two_example_set but ex-1's expected_output is '5' instead of '4' -- a one-byte content change. Must differ from two_example_set's digest.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: example_missing_expected_output
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: expected_output absent from the source example; the function normalizes it to null in the projection rather than omitting the key.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: duplicate_example_ids
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: Two examples share the same example_id with different content. Both entries survive in the preimage, not collapsed into one -- a content digest that silently absorbed a duplicated-row bug would defeat its own purpose. Ordering among same-id rows is a pure function of content (tie-break on the jcs_v1 bytes of each row's own projection), not of input position -- see duplicate_ids_reversed_input_same_digest.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: duplicate_ids_reversed_input_same_digest
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: Same two rows as duplicate_example_ids ('dup'/'first copy'/'a' and 'dup'/'second copy'/'b'), supplied in the OPPOSITE input order. Must equal duplicate_example_ids' digest: the tie-break for same-id rows is the jcs_v1 bytes of each row's own projection, not producer enumeration order, so f(x) == f(x[::-1]) even when ids collide. On the pre-fix implementation (stable sort keyed on example_id alone) this vector produces a DIFFERENT digest from duplicate_example_ids, since a stable sort preserves whichever order the caller supplied for tied keys -- that divergence was the F1 defect this vector pins.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: duplicate_ids_tie_break_by_utf8_bytes_not_utf16
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: Two rows share example_id 'same' with input_text U+1F600 (😀, a UTF-16 surrogate pair) and U+FF21 (Ａ, a single BMP unit). The tie-break for same-id rows is the jcs_v1 UTF-8 BYTES of each row's own projection compared as unsigned bytes: U+FF21 encodes to UTF-8 EF BC A1 and U+1F600 encodes to UTF-8 F0 9F 98 80, so 0xEF < 0xF0 puts the U+FF21 row first. JS pitfall: a naive JavaScript string compare (`a < b` on UTF-16 code units) compares D83D DE00 (U+1F600's surrogate pair) against FF21 (U+FF21's single unit) and finds D83D < FF21, putting U+1F600 first instead -- a DIFFERENT order and therefore a DIFFERENT digest from the one this contract actually produces. This vector's expected_digest is frozen from the function's real output.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: empty_set
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: A dataset version with zero examples still has a well-defined content digest (of the empty array), distinct from every non-empty set above.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: sort_order_utf16_vs_codepoint
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: example_id sort order is UTF-16 code-unit ascending, not Python's default Unicode code-point order. U+1F600 (a surrogate pair D83D DE00 in UTF-16BE, first unit 0xD83D=55357) sorts BEFORE U+FF21 (single unit 0xFF21=65313) under code-unit order, even though by raw code point U+FF21 (65313) < U+1F600 (128512) and would sort first. This vector's expected_digest is the function's actual output (order of the preimage list below is irrelevant -- the function always sorts); the test computes the same projected pair hashed directly in UTF-16 order and in code-point order (bypassing the function's sort) to prove which ordering the const construction actually uses.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: supplementary_plane_example_id
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: F1: two example_ids each containing a supplementary-plane (astral) code point, encoded as a UTF-16 surrogate pair. Each id is encodable text (a complete surrogate pair, not a lone surrogate), so fp2's utf-16 sort-key check accepts both and the digest is computed normally -- this is the positive counterpart to lone_surrogate_example_id_rejected.

dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.name: lone_surrogate_example_id_rejected
dataset_version_content_digest_vectors.description: F1: an example_id containing a lone (unpaired) UTF-16 surrogate is not encodable text -- no two implementations could agree on its UTF-16-BE bytes, so it must never reach the sort key or the hash. This vector has no expected_digest; the corresponding test asserts compute_dataset_version_content_digest raises traigent_schema.fp2.Fp2UnsupportedValue, matching fp2's own rejection of the identical string via fp2.canonicalize.

judge_config_digest_vectors.name: baseline_config
judge_config_digest_vectors.description: The real R2 witness judge config as SUBMITTED in the request body (observability EvaluatorDefinition create/update request judge_config field), verbatim, from the certified-agent-r2 evidence bundle. NOTE (fix round 5, F2): this is the REQUEST shape, not what the Backend persists -- src/services/evaluation_ops_service.py stores payload.judge_config.model_dump(mode='json'), which is JudgeConfig with every optional field present (nulls included); see baseline_config_persisted_shape for the actual persisted/hashed object for this same logical config, and note its digest differs from this one.

judge_config.instructions: Score the agent's answer for exact correctness against the expected output.

judge_config_digest_vectors.name: baseline_config_persisted_shape
judge_config_digest_vectors.description: The SAME logical config as baseline_config (the real R2 witness judge config), but in the shape the Backend actually PERSISTS and therefore actually HASHES: src/services/evaluation_ops_service.py stores payload.judge_config.model_dump(mode='json') of src/shared_infrastructure/schemas/evaluation_ops.py::JudgeConfig, which emits every field -- instructions, model_id, context_type, context_source, parameters, scoring_rubric, response_format_instructions, max_budget -- with unsupplied optionals written as null, not omitted. Seat-measured against the Backend's own model at develop 131af6668. Must differ from baseline_config's digest: the digest preimage is the persisted object, and this producer never stores the absent form of an optional key.

judge_config.instructions: Score the agent's answer for exact correctness against the expected output.

judge_config_digest_vectors.name: baseline_config_key_order_permuted
judge_config_digest_vectors.description: Same keys/values as baseline_config in a different insertion order. Must equal baseline_config's digest: jcs_v1 canonicalization sorts object keys before hashing.

judge_config.instructions: Score the agent's answer for exact correctness against the expected output.

judge_config_digest_vectors.name: baseline_config_value_changed
judge_config_digest_vectors.description: Same as baseline_config with model_id changed from gpt-4o-mini to gpt-4o. Must differ from baseline_config's digest.

judge_config.instructions: Score the agent's answer for exact correctness against the expected output.

judge_config_digest_vectors.name: baseline_config_context_source_null_added
judge_config_digest_vectors.description: Same as baseline_config with context_source explicitly set to null. Must DIFFER from baseline_config's digest: jcs_v1 distinguishes a key absent (baseline_config) from a key present with null (this vector) -- absent != null.

judge_config.instructions: Score the agent's answer for exact correctness against the expected output.

judge_config_digest_vectors.name: full_field_config
judge_config_digest_vectors.description: Uses every JudgeConfig key (observability/evaluator_definition_schema.json#/definitions/JudgeConfig), including nested parameters and scoring_rubric, to prove the whole object -- not a filtered subset -- is hashed.

judge_config.instructions: Score the agent's answer for exact correctness against the expected output.
judge_config.response_format_instructions: Respond with a single float between 0 and 1.

judge_config_digest_vectors.name: empty_config
judge_config_digest_vectors.description: {} is what the Backend's judge_config = db.Column(JSONType, nullable=False, default=dict) persists before an evaluator is configured; the digest must still be well-defined.
